meta.name: Sedgewater Fen
meta.note: Generated by tools/genworld.mjs; safe to hand-edit.

hello.text: Reed. I cut thatch where the sedge grows straight and quiet. That's my place behind me. Come say hello before you let yourself in.

again.text: Dry stems above, wet roots below. Keep them that way.

hello.text: Marsh. I weave traps with openings an eel understands too late. That's my place behind me. Come say hello before you let yourself in.

again.text: Nothing in the basket yet. That is how waiting looks.

text: Stay on the boards until you know it. Everyone says that. Everyone means it.
Meg. I have been getting across this fen for forty years and I still go the long way.

third.text: Still on the boards, I see. Sensible.

choices.text: Why can I not cut across?
What is out past the reeds?
I will find my own way.

text: Because the channels come right up the middle and only the middle joins them.
Two doors a hundred paces apart, and the walk between them goes past my feet. That is a fen.

out.text: More of it. It is ankle deep for a day in any direction and then it is over your head.

trade.text: Alder, is it. Boards want mending oftener than you would think. There.

text: You walked all the way out here. Nobody walks all the way out here.
Quill. Reed cutter. The hut is yours to sit in now, it is dry in one corner.
One corner. I want to be clear about the number.

welcome.text: Come in. Mind the bundles, and mind the hole.

holeagain.text: You have been hauling my trap. Good. It goes sour if nobody lifts it.

choices.text: Does the water ever go down?
There is a hole in your floor.
Which corner is the dry one?
I have sticks, if reed is short.

gift.text: Marsh marigold, off the bank. Take them before the wet gets in.

text: It goes down in August and everyone gets ambitious and cuts a new path across.
Then it comes back up in September and takes the path, and we all pretend we knew.
The hut is on posts and the fen is under it, so the fen may as well be in it. The trap hangs through.
Haul it when you are in there. It is bad manners to leave a trap down and worse to leave it up.
East end, up the step. That step is the difference between a house and a boat and I built it myself.
Everything I care about is on it. Everything I use is not.

trade.text: Willow? I will have that. Reed will not take a nail and some days that matters.

text: You are the new one. We could see your roof before we could reach it.
Tarn. Nearest neighbour you have got, which out here means about a quarter of an hour.

fourth.text: Still nearest. Still a quarter of an hour.

shop.text: The Staithe. Follow the boards to the middle and take the next spur but one.

trade.text: Hard standing is worth money in a bog. I will take those.
